journal.title: Trading journal
journal.intro: Write down why you buy or sell. Two weeks later we’ll ask whether it played out: that way you learn from your decisions, not just the results.
journal.whyHint: Pick a reason and we’ll note it in your journal.
journal.willRemind: We’ll note it in your journal. In 14 days we’ll ask if it played out.
journal.linkHint: Note why you buy and check whether you were right
journal.dueCount: {n, plural, one {# entry to review} other {# entries to review}}

journal.summaryBuy: Your buys {why}: {met} of {n} went as you expected.
journal.summarySell: Your sells {why}: {met} of {n} went as you expected.
journal.summaryNote: With only a few entries it’s too early to draw conclusions. The value is in seeing the pattern over time.
journal.emptyBody: Next time you buy or sell, pick why in the order sheet.

sell.CHANGED: I no longer believe in it
sell.NEED_CASH: I want the money for something else

buy.QUALITY: because you believed in the company

sell.CHANGED: because you stopped believing in it
sell.FEAR: out of fear it would fall

buy.QUALITY: Believing in a company is fine if you know why. Write down what would have to happen for you to stop believing in it, and look for the case against too: it’s the antidote to confirmation bias.
buy.CHEAP: Anchoring: falling doesn’t make it cheap. Cheap means paying less than the business is worth, and that’s measured by its earnings, not by the old price.
buy.DIVERSIFY: Spreading out softens the blow of a single fall. Check they don’t all move together: diversifying means owning different things, not many similar ones.
buy.LONG_TERM: Thinking long term helps you not react to every dip. The hard part is sticking to the plan when it falls: decide today what you’d do after a 20 % drop.
buy.NEWS: Once news is public, the price has usually priced it in within minutes. Ask yourself what you know that the market doesn’t already.
buy.SOCIAL: FOMO and herd behaviour: buying because others are buying usually means getting in late. Whoever recommends it online loses nothing if it goes wrong for you.
buy.HUNCH: Overconfidence: a hunch feels certain, but it isn’t a reason. Writing it down and reviewing it will show you how often your hunches are actually right.
buy.OTHER: Writing down your reason is already a good habit: in two weeks you’ll be able to check whether you were right.

sell.TARGET: Selling at your target is following a plan. Watch out for the disposition effect: selling winners early and holding on to losers.
sell.CHANGED: Selling because your reason has changed is consistent. What matters is the business today, not what you paid.
sell.REBALANCE: Rebalancing takes your portfolio back to the mix you chose: you sell some of what rose most without trying to guess the future.
sell.NEED_CASH: Moving money to another idea makes sense if the new one is better than the one you’re leaving, not just more exciting.
sell.FEAR: Loss aversion: the fear of losing more pushes you to sell at the worst moment. Ask yourself whether you’d buy it today at this price.
sell.NEWS: Selling after the news usually comes too late: prices react within minutes. Ask whether the business changed or just the day’s mood.
sell.SOCIAL: Herd behaviour: selling because others sell is still following the crowd, just on the way out.
sell.HUNCH: A hunch to get out is as unreliable as one to get in. Write it down and check it: that’s how you’ll know how often you’re right.
sell.OTHER: Writing down your reason is already a good habit: in two weeks you’ll be able to check whether you were right.
